- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–4% to align with sentiment.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if price is deviating from 30-day moving average, forecast should converge toward it within 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overfits recent volatility; dampen forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish, model delays correction; apply a 1–3 day lag in adjusting downward trend.
- If sentiment is bullish but price is flat or slightly declining, model often overreacts — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid false momentum.
